task_2.title: Support progress bar output when capture is disabled
task_2.description: Previously, pytest suppressed progress output (percentage or count) whenever capture was disabled (capture=no), because uncaptured test output could intermingle with the progress line. A new console_output_style value, 'progress-even-when-capture-no', overrides this suppression so users of large test suites who disable capture for performance reasons can still see progress information.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: When running pytest with capture disabled (capture=no), progress bar information is unconditionally suppressed. For large test suites where disabling capture is necessary for performance, users lose all visual progress feedback. Ensure that a new console_output_style option value allows users to explicitly opt in to progress output even when capture is disabled.

expectation.grounded: The console_output_style ini option must accept the value 'progress-even-when-capture-no' in addition to the existing 'progress', 'count', and 'classic' values. When this value is set, _determine_show_progress_info on TerminalReporter must return 'progress' even when the capture option is 'no'. When console_output_style is set to any other value and capture is 'no', progress information must still be suppressed as before. The setupshow guard must remain unaffected.
expectation.conceptual: A new configuration value for console_output_style allows users to force progress bar display even when output capture is disabled. When this value is configured, pytest displays percentage-based progress information during test runs regardless of the capture setting. All other console_output_style values retain their existing behavior with respect to capture.

constraints.grounded: The default value for console_output_style must remain 'progress'. Existing behavior where capture=no suppresses progress output must be preserved unless the user explicitly opts in via the new value. The setupshow check must continue to independently suppress progress regardless of console_output_style. The 'count' and 'classic' styles must be unaffected by this change.
constraints.conceptual: The default behavior must not change; progress is still hidden when capture is off unless the user explicitly enables the new option. Other output styles and other conditions that suppress progress must remain unaffected.

behavior: When console_output_style is set to 'progress-even-when-capture-no' and capture is 'no', progress information is displayed as percentage-based progress (same as the 'progress' style).
When console_output_style is set to 'progress' and capture is 'no', progress information remains suppressed (existing behavior preserved).
When console_output_style is set to 'progress-even-when-capture-no' and capture is enabled, progress information is displayed identically to the 'progress' style.
When setupshow is enabled, progress information is suppressed regardless of console_output_style value.
The ini option help text reflects the availability of the new value.
acceptance_criteria: When console_output_style is set to 'progress-even-when-capture-no' and capture=no, the test session displays progress percentage output.
When console_output_style is set to 'progress' and capture=no, no progress output is shown (regression guard).
When console_output_style is set to 'progress-even-when-capture-no' and capture is enabled, progress output is shown identically to the 'progress' style.
When console_output_style is set to 'count' and capture=no, count-style output is still suppressed (regression guard).
When setupshow is active, progress is suppressed regardless of the console_output_style value.
The default value of console_output_style remains 'progress'.

task_1.title: Support test discovery for @classmethod-decorated test methods
task_1.description: Previously, pytest's test collection silently skipped methods decorated with @classmethod—they were never discovered or run, with no warning emitted. This was inconsistent with @staticmethod-decorated methods, which were already discoverable. The fix extends the test discovery logic to unwrap classmethod descriptors in the same way staticmethod descriptors are unwrapped, so @classmethod test methods are now collected and executed following the same rules as normal test methods.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that test methods decorated with @classmethod inside test classes are discovered and collected by pytest during test collection, rather than being silently skipped. Previously, @staticmethod test methods were discoverable but @classmethod test methods were not, leading to tests that appeared to exist in source code but never ran—with no warning or error to alert the user.

expectation.grounded: The PyCollector.istestfunction method must recognize classmethod descriptors in addition to staticmethod descriptors. When a classmethod is encountered during collection, its underlying callable must be unwrapped (via the __func__ attribute) and evaluated for callability and fixture markers, just as staticmethod descriptors are. After unwrapping, standard test name filtering (funcnamefilter) and nose-test detection (isnosetest) rules apply. The method should return True for valid @classmethod test methods that pass name filtering and are not fixture-decorated.
expectation.conceptual: When a test class contains methods decorated with @classmethod whose names match the test naming convention, pytest should discover and collect them as runnable tests. The discovery behavior for @classmethod methods should be consistent with how @staticmethod methods are already discovered. No silent omission of valid test methods should occur.

constraints.grounded: Existing discovery of @staticmethod-decorated test methods must remain unaffected. The unwrapping logic must safely handle descriptors that lack a __func__ attribute (via safe_getattr fallback). Methods that do not pass funcnamefilter or isnosetest checks must still be excluded. Methods with fixture markers (getfixturemarker returning non-None) must still be excluded. Non-callable objects must still be excluded after unwrapping.
constraints.conceptual: The change must not alter the discovery behavior of any previously collected tests (static methods, regular methods, or non-test methods). Only @classmethod-decorated methods that were previously silently skipped should now be additionally discovered. All existing filtering rules (name patterns, fixture exclusion, callability) must continue to apply uniformly.

behavior: A @classmethod-decorated method inside a test class whose name matches the test naming pattern (e.g., test_*) is now collected as a test item during pytest collection.
The classmethod descriptor is unwrapped to its underlying function before callability and fixture marker checks are performed.
If the classmethod's underlying function is callable and has no fixture marker, istestfunction returns True for it.
If the classmethod's underlying function has a fixture marker, it is excluded from collection, consistent with existing behavior for regular and static methods.
Previously silently skipped @classmethod tests now appear in test collection output (e.g., pytest --collect-only and verbose mode).
@staticmethod discovery behavior remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a test class contains a @classmethod-decorated method named 'test_example', running pytest --collect-only should list it as a collected test item.
When a test class contains a @classmethod-decorated test method, running pytest should execute that test and report its result (pass/fail).
When a @classmethod test method uses assertions, failures should be reported just like failures in regular test methods.
When a @classmethod and a @staticmethod test exist in the same class, both should be discovered and run.
When a @classmethod-decorated method does NOT match the test naming convention, it should not be collected as a test.
When a regular (non-decorated) test method exists alongside @classmethod tests, the regular method's discovery and execution should be unaffected.

When a @classmethod test is parametrized with the decorator in the correct order (@classmethod on the inside, @pytest.mark.parametrize on the outside), it should be collected with all parameter variants.

task_5.title: Report all teardown errors via ExceptionGroup instead of discarding all but the first
task_5.description: Previously, when multiple errors occurred during test teardown (e.g., multiple fixture finalizers failing), only the first exception was captured and reported to the user while the rest were silently discarded. This change collects all teardown exceptions and, when more than one occurs, raises them together as a BaseExceptionGroup so that every failure is visible in the test report.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when multiple exceptions are raised during test teardown, all of them are reported to the user rather than silently discarding every exception except the first. Previously, if several fixture finalizers or teardown steps failed, only the first error surfaced, making it difficult to diagnose cascading or independent teardown failures.

expectation.grounded: When the SetupState teardown encounters multiple exceptions across finalizers, it must collect all exceptions. If a single node's finalizers produce multiple exceptions, they are wrapped in a BaseExceptionGroup. If multiple nodes each produce exceptions during a single teardown pass, the individual exceptions (or per-node BaseExceptionGroups) are aggregated into a top-level BaseExceptionGroup. When only a single exception occurs across the entire teardown, it must be raised directly without wrapping in an ExceptionGroup. On Python versions below 3.11, the exceptiongroup backport package provides BaseExceptionGroup.
expectation.conceptual: When test teardown produces multiple errors, all errors must be reported to the user grouped together, rather than only showing the first and silently dropping the rest. When only a single error occurs during teardown, it should be raised as-is without any additional wrapping.

constraints.grounded: A single teardown exception must be raised directly as that exception type, not wrapped in a BaseExceptionGroup. The ordering of exceptions within a BaseExceptionGroup must preserve the original execution order of the finalizers. The behavior must be compatible with Python versions below 3.11 by using the exceptiongroup backport. Only exceptions matching TEST_OUTCOME should be caught and collected; other exception types must propagate normally.
constraints.conceptual: Single-error teardown behavior must remain unchanged from prior versions. Multi-error grouping must not alter the exception types of individual errors or lose any error information. The feature must work across all supported Python versions.

behavior: When one finalizer fails during teardown for a single node, that exception is raised directly without any wrapping.
When multiple finalizers fail during teardown for a single node, those exceptions are collected and wrapped in a BaseExceptionGroup scoped to that node.
When teardown of multiple nodes each produces exceptions, all per-node exceptions (or per-node ExceptionGroups) are aggregated into a single top-level BaseExceptionGroup.
Exceptions within each group are ordered to reflect the original finalizer execution order.
On Python < 3.11, BaseExceptionGroup is sourced from the exceptiongroup backport package.
Previously, only the first exception was retained and all subsequent teardown exceptions were silently discarded.
acceptance_criteria: When a single finalizer raises an exception during teardown, the exception is raised directly and its type and message are preserved exactly.
When two or more finalizers for the same fixture/node raise exceptions during teardown, a BaseExceptionGroup is raised containing all individual exceptions.
When finalizers across multiple nodes raise exceptions during teardown, a top-level BaseExceptionGroup is raised that nests the per-node exceptions.
Given a teardown where no exceptions occur, no exception is raised and teardown completes normally.
The exception group contains all raised exceptions with none silently discarded.
On Python < 3.11, the BaseExceptionGroup from the exceptiongroup backport behaves equivalently to the built-in version on Python 3.11+.

task_3.title: Add --log-disable CLI option to selectively disable loggers
task_3.description: A new --log-disable command-line option is introduced to allow users to selectively disable individual loggers by name during test execution. This addresses the common need to suppress excessive or noisy logging output from specific loggers without patching project code. The option can be passed multiple times to disable multiple loggers. When specified, the named loggers are disabled at plugin initialization time via the standard Python logging facility.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: During test runs, certain loggers may produce excessive or irrelevant log output that obscures useful information. Users currently have no built-in way to selectively silence specific loggers from the command line. Ensure that pytest provides a CLI option to disable one or more loggers by name, so that users can suppress noisy loggers without modifying application code or writing custom plugins.

expectation.grounded: A new --log-disable CLI option is available on the pytest command line, registered under the logging option group. The option accepts a logger name as its argument, uses append semantics so it can be specified multiple times, and defaults to an empty list. When one or more logger names are provided, the LoggingPlugin retrieves each named logger via logging.getLogger and sets its disabled attribute to True during plugin initialization. If no --log-disable arguments are provided, no loggers are affected and existing behavior is preserved.
expectation.conceptual: Users can pass --log-disable <logger_name> on the pytest command line to silence a specific logger. The option may be repeated to disable multiple loggers. Disabled loggers produce no output during the test session. When the option is not used, all logging behavior remains unchanged.

constraints.grounded: The --log-disable option must not interfere with other logging-related CLI options (--log-level, --log-format, --log-cli-level, --log-file, --log-auto-indent). Loggers not named in --log-disable must remain fully operational. The option must use append action so that multiple loggers can be disabled independently. The default value must be an empty list, ensuring no loggers are disabled when the option is omitted. Logger disabling must occur during LoggingPlugin initialization, before any test collection or execution logging occurs.
constraints.conceptual: Disabling specific loggers must not affect any other logging configuration or other loggers. The feature must be additive and opt-in, with no impact on existing test runs that do not use the new option. Logger suppression must take effect before tests begin executing.

behavior: When --log-disable is passed with a logger name, that logger is disabled and produces no log output for the duration of the test session.
When --log-disable is passed multiple times with different logger names, all specified loggers are independently disabled.
When --log-disable is not passed, no loggers are disabled and all logging behavior is identical to previous versions.
The --log-disable option appears in pytest --help output under the logging option group.
Logger disabling takes effect at plugin initialization, before test collection and execution begin.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs pytest with --log-disable <logger_name>, log records from that logger should not appear in any log output (console, file, or captured).
When a user runs pytest with --log-disable foo --log-disable bar, both the 'foo' and 'bar' loggers should be disabled and produce no output.
When a user runs pytest without --log-disable, all loggers should function normally and produce output as configured by other logging options.
When a user runs pytest --help, the --log-disable option should be listed with a description indicating it disables a logger by name and can be passed multiple times.
When --log-disable targets a logger that has child loggers, only the explicitly named logger is disabled; child logger behavior follows standard Python logging propagation rules.
When --log-disable is combined with other logging options such as --log-level or --log-cli-level, the other options continue to function correctly for all non-disabled loggers.

task_4.title: Add tmp_path retention count and policy configuration options
task_4.description: Introduces two new pytest configuration options, tmp_path_retention_count and tmp_path_retention_policy, that give users fine-grained control over how temporary directories created by the tmp_path fixture are retained across sessions. Previously, pytest unconditionally kept the last 3 root temporary directories for every test. With this change, users can choose to retain directories only for failed tests (saving significant disk space for data-heavy test suites), retain all directories as before, or retain none. Session-level and per-test cleanup is performed automatically based on the configured policy, and dead symlinks in the base temp directory are cleaned up as well.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the tmp_path fixture supports configurable retention of temporary directories via two new ini-style configuration options: tmp_path_retention_count (controlling how many session-level base directories are kept) and tmp_path_retention_policy (controlling which per-test directories are kept based on test outcome). Previously, pytest unconditionally kept the last 3 root temporary directories regardless of test outcome, which wasted significant disk space for test suites that manipulate large amounts of data in temporary directories.

expectation.grounded: A new ini option tmp_path_retention_count (integer, default 3) controls the number of past session base temporary directories to retain. A new ini option tmp_path_retention_policy (one of 'all', 'failed', 'none', default 'all') controls which per-test temporary directories are retained. TempPathFactory must accept retention_count and retention_policy in its constructor and its from_config class method must read and validate them. When tmp_path_retention_count is negative, a ValueError must be raised. When tmp_path_retention_policy is not one of the three allowed values, a ValueError must be raised. When policy is 'failed', per-test temporary directories for passing tests must be removed during fixture teardown. When policy is 'failed' and all tests in a session pass, the entire session base directory must be removed at session finish (unless a custom --basetemp was specified). When policy is 'none', the keep parameter for session directory cleanup must be set to 0, and no cleanup locks should be created. Dead symlinks in the base temp directory must be cleaned up after directory removal. The tmp_path fixture must yield the path rather than return it, enabling teardown logic to execute after the test completes. Test outcomes must be tracked per-item via a stash key and the pytest_runtest_makereport hook.
expectation.conceptual: Users can configure how many session-level temporary directories pytest retains and under what conditions per-test directories are kept. The 'all' policy preserves every test's temporary directory (backward-compatible default). The 'failed' policy retains directories only for failing tests, automatically removing directories for passing tests after the test completes and removing the entire session directory if all tests pass. The 'none' policy retains no temporary directories beyond the current session. Invalid configuration values must be rejected with clear errors at startup.

constraints.grounded: The default value of tmp_path_retention_count must be 3 and tmp_path_retention_policy must be 'all', preserving full backward compatibility with prior behavior. The tmp_path fixture must continue to provide a unique pathlib.Path per test invocation. Directory removal must be best-effort (ignoring errors from leaked resources or permission issues). When --basetemp is explicitly provided by the user, session-level cleanup for the 'failed' policy must not remove the user-specified base directory. The cleanup_numbered_dir function must gracefully handle the case where the root directory does not exist. Cleanup lock creation must be skipped when keep is 0.
constraints.conceptual: Existing test suites that do not set the new options must behave identically to before the change. Temporary directory removal must be resilient and not cause test failures due to cleanup errors. User-specified base temp directories must not be silently deleted by automatic retention policies.

behavior: When tmp_path_retention_policy is set to 'all' (the default), all per-test temporary directories are retained, matching the previous behavior.
When tmp_path_retention_policy is set to 'failed', per-test temporary directories for passing tests are removed during fixture teardown via best-effort rmtree.

When tmp_path_retention_policy is set to 'failed' and all tests pass in a session (exit status 0), the entire session base temporary directory is removed at session finish, unless --basetemp was explicitly set.
When tmp_path_retention_policy is set to 'none', the keep parameter is set to 0, no cleanup locks are created, and no past session directories are retained.
When tmp_path_retention_count is set to a non-negative integer, that value replaces the previously hardcoded keep count of 3 for session base directory retention.
When tmp_path_retention_count is set to a negative value, a ValueError is raised during configuration.
When tmp_path_retention_policy is set to an invalid value (not 'all', 'failed', or 'none'), a ValueError is raised during configuration.
Dead symlinks in the base temp directory are cleaned up after directory removal and during numbered directory cleanup.
The tmp_path fixture now yields the path (generator-based), allowing post-test teardown logic to execute after the test body completes.

Test pass/fail outcomes are tracked per-item via a stash key populated by the pytest_runtest_makereport hook, enabling the retention policy logic to determine whether a test's directory should be retained.
acceptance_criteria: When no retention options are configured, the tmp_path fixture should behave identically to the previous version, retaining 3 session directories and all per-test directories.
When tmp_path_retention_policy is set to 'failed' and a test passes, the test's temporary directory should be removed after the test completes.
When tmp_path_retention_policy is set to 'failed' and a test fails, the test's temporary directory should be preserved for debugging.
When tmp_path_retention_policy is set to 'failed' and all tests in the session pass, the session base temporary directory should be removed at session finish.
When tmp_path_retention_policy is set to 'failed' and --basetemp is explicitly provided, the session base directory should not be removed even if all tests pass.
When tmp_path_retention_policy is set to 'none', no past session directories should be retained and no cleanup locks should be created.
When tmp_path_retention_count is set to a positive integer N, exactly the last N session base directories should be retained.
When tmp_path_retention_count is set to a negative integer, a ValueError should be raised at configuration time.
When tmp_path_retention_policy is set to an unrecognized string, a ValueError should be raised at configuration time.
When temporary directory removal fails due to permission errors or leaked resources, the failure should be silently ignored and not cause the test run to fail.
Dead symlinks in the base temp directory should be cleaned up after per-test directory removal and during numbered directory cleanup.

task_7.title: Add start and stop timestamps to TestReport objects
task_7.description: TestReport objects previously only contained a duration field, making it impossible to correlate test results with external events by wall-clock time. This change adds start and stop timestamp attributes to TestReport, populated from the underlying CallInfo object, so that consumers of test reports (e.g., report-log parsers, CI integrations) can determine exactly when each test phase began and ended.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that TestReport objects expose start and stop timestamps (seconds since the epoch) for each test phase (setup, call, teardown), so that users consuming pytest reports can correlate test execution windows with external events and logs.

expectation.grounded: TestReport gains two new public float attributes, `start` and `stop`, representing system time in seconds since the epoch. The `TestReport.__init__` constructor accepts optional `start` and `stop` keyword arguments defaulting to 0. The `TestReport.from_item_and_call` class method propagates the `start` and `stop` values from the CallInfo object into the constructed TestReport. These attributes are included in the report's serialized representation alongside the existing `duration` field.
expectation.conceptual: Each TestReport instance carries wall-clock timestamps indicating when the corresponding test phase started and stopped. These timestamps are automatically populated when reports are created from test execution and default to zero when not explicitly provided.

constraints.grounded: The existing `duration` attribute and all other TestReport attributes must remain unchanged and unaffected. The `start` and `stop` parameters must default to 0 so that existing code constructing TestReport objects directly without supplying timestamps continues to work without modification. The `start` and `stop` values must originate from CallInfo.start and CallInfo.stop respectively when constructed via `from_item_and_call`.
constraints.conceptual: Adding timestamps must not break any existing TestReport construction patterns or alter the existing duration semantics. Code that does not use the new attributes should be completely unaffected. The timestamps must reflect actual system wall-clock time, not relative offsets.

behavior: TestReport objects created via `from_item_and_call` now carry `start` and `stop` float attributes sourced from the CallInfo object, representing epoch-based system timestamps.
TestReport objects constructed directly via `__init__` accept optional `start` and `stop` keyword arguments, both defaulting to 0.
The `start` and `stop` attributes appear in each test phase report (setup, call, teardown) independently, reflecting the timing of that specific phase.
Serialized report representations (e.g., reportlog JSON output) include the new `start` and `stop` fields alongside the existing `duration` field.
acceptance_criteria: When a test runs to completion, the resulting TestReport for the 'call' phase should have a `start` attribute that is a positive float representing seconds since the epoch.

When a test runs to completion, the resulting TestReport for the 'call' phase should have a `stop` attribute that is a positive float representing seconds since the epoch, and `stop` should be greater than or equal to `start`.
When a TestReport is created via `from_item_and_call`, its `start` and `stop` values should match the corresponding CallInfo object's `start` and `stop` values.
When a TestReport is constructed directly without providing `start` or `stop`, both attributes should default to 0.
Given a test with setup, call, and teardown phases, each phase's TestReport should independently carry its own `start` and `stop` timestamps reflecting that phase's execution window.
When the TestReport is serialized (e.g., via reportlog), the `start` and `stop` fields should be present in the output alongside `duration`.
Existing code that constructs or consumes TestReport objects without referencing `start` or `stop` should continue to function without error or behavioral change.

task_8.title: Split report header into separate lines for rootdir, configfile, and testpaths
task_8.description: The pytest session report header previously displayed rootdir, configfile, and testpaths as a single comma-separated line, making it difficult to read. This change splits them so that each piece of configuration metadata is printed on its own dedicated line in the terminal output, improving readability of the test session header.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the pytest report header displays rootdir, configfile, and testpaths on separate lines instead of concatenating them into a single comma-delimited line. The previous format crammed all configuration metadata together, making it hard to scan and read quickly during test runs.

expectation.grounded: The pytest_report_header hook on TerminalReporter must return a list where rootdir, configfile, and testpaths are each separate string entries rather than being joined into a single string. The rootdir entry should always be present. The configfile entry should only appear when config.inipath is set. The testpaths entry should only appear when the args source is Config.ArgsSource.TESTPATHS. Each entry is rendered on its own line in the terminal output.
expectation.conceptual: When a pytest session starts, each piece of configuration metadata (root directory, configuration file path, and test paths) should be displayed on its own line in the session header, rather than being combined into one line. Optional fields like configfile and testpaths should only appear when they are relevant to the current session configuration.

constraints.grounded: The rootdir line must always be present in the report header output. The configfile line must only appear when an ini configuration file is detected (config.inipath is truthy). The testpaths line must only appear when args_source equals Config.ArgsSource.TESTPATHS. The plugin information line that follows must remain unaffected. The labels 'rootdir:', 'configfile:', and 'testpaths:' must be preserved. No other report header content (e.g., plugin listing) should be altered.
constraints.conceptual: The information content and conditional display logic for each metadata field must remain the same as before—only the presentation layout changes from one combined line to multiple separate lines. No configuration metadata should be lost or newly introduced. Plugin information reporting must not be affected.

behavior: rootdir is always displayed as its own line in the session header, formatted as 'rootdir: <path>'
configfile is displayed as a separate line 'configfile: <relative path>' only when an ini configuration file is present
testpaths is displayed as a separate line 'testpaths: <comma-separated paths>' only when test paths are the source of test arguments
Previously all three fields were concatenated into a single comma-separated line; now each is an independent line
The number of header lines returned by pytest_report_header varies from 1 to 3 depending on which optional fields are active, plus the plugin info line if plugins are present
acceptance_criteria: When running pytest with only a rootdir and no config file or testpaths, the header should show a single line 'rootdir: <path>' without any trailing comma-separated fields
When running pytest with a rootdir and a config file, the header should show 'rootdir: <path>' on one line and 'configfile: <relative path>' on the next line
When running pytest with rootdir, config file, and testpaths configured, the header should show three separate lines: one for rootdir, one for configfile, and one for testpaths
When running pytest with rootdir and testpaths but no config file, the header should show 'rootdir: <path>' on one line and 'testpaths: <paths>' on a separate line, with no configfile line
The plugin metadata line should continue to appear on its own separate line, unaffected by this change

task_6.title: Allow spaces in -p plugin arguments for pytest CLI and config
task_6.description: The -p flag for enabling or disabling pytest plugins previously required the value to be either a separate token or concatenated without spaces (e.g., -pno:logging). This change allows a space between -p and the plugin value (e.g., -p no:logging), making it more intuitive to specify plugin arguments in configuration files such as the addopts list in pyproject.toml.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: When specifying plugin arguments via the -p flag in pytest configuration files (e.g., the addopts list), users must either split the flag and value into two separate list entries or concatenate them without a space. This is inconsistent with most other pytest CLI arguments that accept --arg=value or --arg value forms. Ensure that the -p flag accepts a space between the flag and its value (e.g., "-p no:logging") so that configuration files can use a single, readable entry per plugin directive.

expectation.grounded: PytestPluginManager must strip leading and trailing whitespace from the parsed plugin argument before passing it to consider_pluginarg. When -p is provided with a trailing space before the value (e.g., "-p no:logging"), the plugin manager should correctly resolve the plugin name and apply it identically to the concatenated form ("-pno:logging"). Both plugin enabling (e.g., "-p myplugin") and plugin disabling (e.g., "-p no:myplugin") must work with the space-separated format.
expectation.conceptual: The -p flag should accept an optional space between the flag and its plugin value. The resulting behavior for plugin loading and disabling must be identical regardless of whether the space is present. This applies to both direct CLI invocation and configuration-file-based addopts entries.

constraints.grounded: Existing concatenated forms ("-pno:logging", "-pmyplugin") and two-token forms ("-p", "no:logging") must continue to work without regression. The consider_pluginarg method must receive the same cleaned plugin name regardless of input format. The exclude_only filtering logic (checking for the "no:" prefix) must not be affected by residual whitespace.
constraints.conceptual: All previously supported formats for specifying -p arguments must remain valid and produce identical behavior. No existing plugin loading or disabling functionality should break. The change must be purely additive, enabling a new accepted format without altering semantics of existing ones.

behavior: When a -p argument is provided as a single string with a space between the flag and value (e.g., "-p no:logging"), the whitespace is stripped and the plugin argument is processed normally.
Plugin disable directives using the "no:" prefix work correctly with the space-separated form (e.g., "-p no:logging" disables the logging plugin).
Plugin enable directives work correctly with the space-separated form (e.g., "-p myplugin" enables the plugin).
The concatenated form without space ("-pno:logging") continues to work identically as before.
Arguments specified in the addopts configuration list using the space-separated format are parsed and applied correctly.
acceptance_criteria: When addopts is configured with ["-p no:logging"] (space between -p and no:logging), the logging plugin should be disabled, identical to using ["-pno:logging"].
When addopts is configured with ["-p myplugin"] (space between -p and plugin name), the specified plugin should be loaded.
When -p is passed on the CLI as a single quoted argument with a space (e.g., '-p no:logging'), the plugin should be correctly disabled.
When -p is passed in the existing concatenated form (-pno:logging), behavior must remain unchanged from prior versions.
When -p is passed as two separate tokens (-p no:logging as separate arguments), behavior must remain unchanged from prior versions.

Given a configuration with extra whitespace around the plugin name in the -p argument (e.g., "-p  no:logging" with extra spaces), the plugin argument should still be resolved correctly after stripping.

task_9.title: Fix crash in traceback formatting when AST has pathological position attributes
task_9.description: pytest crashes with an INTERNALERROR (IndexError: list index out of range) when formatting tracebacks for test failures whose AST nodes carry pathological or invalid position attributes. This can occur with alternative Python front-ends such as Hylang that sometimes produce AST with incorrect or missing source positions. The fix ensures that FormattedExcinfo.get_source properly handles all out-of-range line indices—including negative indices that remain out of bounds after adjustment—by falling back to a safe placeholder source instead of crashing.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest does not crash with an INTERNALERROR when formatting tracebacks for test code whose AST nodes have pathological position attributes (e.g., zero-length source, negative or excessively large line numbers). Instead, pytest should gracefully degrade and display a placeholder representation for the unresolvable source line, allowing the test session to complete and report results normally.

expectation.grounded: When FormattedExcinfo.get_source receives a line_index that is negative, it should first attempt to resolve it as a Python-style negative index relative to the source length. After resolution, if the index is still out of range (negative or >= len(source.lines)), or if source is None, the method should fall back to a placeholder Source containing '???' with line_index reset to 0. The method must never raise an IndexError regardless of the line_index value provided.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest encounters a traceback entry whose source line cannot be determined due to invalid position information, it should substitute a safe placeholder in the failure report rather than crashing. The test session should continue running subsequent tests and exit with proper test result reporting.

constraints.grounded: Negative line indices that are within the valid range of source.lines (i.e., -len(source.lines) <= line_index < 0) must still resolve correctly via Python-style negative indexing before any fallback is applied. The fallback to placeholder source must only activate when the index is genuinely unresolvable. Existing traceback formatting behavior for valid source positions must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Normal traceback formatting for standard Python code must not be affected. The fix must only change behavior for edge cases involving invalid or out-of-range position attributes. Test sessions must never terminate with an INTERNALERROR due to unresolvable source positions in traceback entries.

behavior: Negative line_index values are resolved relative to source length before bounds checking, rather than after.
After negative index resolution, if line_index is still negative (e.g., the absolute value exceeds source length), the method falls back to placeholder source '???' with line_index 0.
If line_index >= len(source.lines), the method falls back to placeholder source '???' with line_index 0 (existing behavior preserved).
If source is None, the method falls back to placeholder source '???' with line_index 0 (existing behavior preserved).
The INTERNALERROR / IndexError on source.lines[line_index] is eliminated for all possible line_index values.
acceptance_criteria: When a test produces a traceback with AST nodes having a line number of 0 (resulting in a negative or zero line_index for source lookup), pytest should display '???' as the source line in the failure report instead of crashing.
When a test produces a traceback with AST nodes having line numbers exceeding the actual source length, pytest should display '???' as the source line in the failure report instead of crashing.

When running tests written in an alternative front-end (e.g., Hylang) that generates AST with incorrect position attributes, pytest should complete the test session and report pass/fail results without INTERNALERROR.

When running standard Python tests with valid source positions, traceback formatting should remain identical to previous behavior, including correct resolution of negative line indices within valid range.
Given a source with N lines and a line_index of -(N+1) or smaller, pytest should fall back to the placeholder source rather than raising an IndexError.

task_10.title: Avoid assertion output truncation when truncation message is longer than hidden text and fix hidden line count
task_10.description: When a test assertion failure output was close to the truncation limit, pytest would truncate the output and replace it with a truncation message that was actually longer than the hidden content, resulting in a net increase in verbosity rather than a reduction. Additionally, the reported number of hidden lines in the truncation message was inaccurate—it could overcount by one due to always accounting for a part-truncated final line even when no characters were removed from it. This change makes truncation aware of the size of the truncation message itself, skipping truncation entirely when it would make the output longer, and corrects the hidden line count to accurately reflect how many lines were actually removed.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest assertion output truncation does not produce output that is longer than the original untruncated output. When the truncation explanation message (including the '...Full output truncated (N lines hidden)' notice) would be equal to or longer than the content it replaces, the full output should be shown instead. Additionally, ensure that the reported number of hidden lines in the truncation message is accurate and does not overcount lines that were not actually removed.

expectation.grounded: The _truncate_explanation function should compare the input size against 'tolerable' limits that account for the overhead of the truncation message itself (approximately 70 extra characters and 2 extra lines beyond the configured max_chars and max_lines). If the input fits within these tolerable limits, the function returns the full untruncated input_lines. When truncation does occur, the hidden line count should only include an extra line for the part-truncated final line when character-level truncation was actually applied to that line. The pluralization of 'line'/'lines' in the truncation message must match the actual truncated_line_count. The _truncate_by_char_count helper no longer performs its own early-return check since the caller handles that decision.
expectation.conceptual: When assertion failure output is close to the truncation threshold, pytest should compare the cost of truncating (adding the truncation notice) against the cost of showing the full output, and choose whichever is shorter. The number of hidden lines reported in the truncation message should exactly match the number of lines actually removed from the output, accounting correctly for whether the final visible line was partially truncated or shown in full.

constraints.grounded: The default truncation limits (DEFAULT_MAX_LINES and DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS) must remain unchanged. Output that significantly exceeds the limits (beyond the tolerable threshold) must still be truncated as before. The truncation message format ('...Full output truncated (N line(s) hidden), use '-vv' to show') must be preserved. The ellipsis ('...') must still be appended to the last visible line when truncation occurs. The _truncate_by_char_count function must still correctly identify and truncate at the character boundary when character-level truncation is needed.
constraints.conceptual: Truncation behavior for outputs that clearly exceed the limits must remain unchanged. Only outputs near the boundary where truncation would be counterproductive should be affected. The user-facing truncation message format and the suggestion to use '-vv' must be preserved. No existing truncation behavior for large outputs should regress.

behavior: When assertion output is within approximately 70 characters and 2 lines of the truncation limits, the full output is displayed instead of being truncated.
When truncation does occur and the final visible line was not character-truncated, the hidden line count no longer includes an extra line for the final line.
When truncation occurs and the final visible line was character-truncated, the hidden line count correctly includes the extra line.
After line-based truncation, character-based truncation is only applied if the remaining lines still exceed the tolerable character limit.
When the last line after line truncation is empty, the ellipsis replaces it as '...' instead of appending to it.
The truncation message correctly uses singular 'line' when exactly 1 line is hidden and plural 'lines' otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: When a test assertion output is only 1-2 lines and a few characters beyond the truncation limit, the full output is shown without any truncation message.
When a test assertion output significantly exceeds the truncation limit, it is truncated and the truncation message is displayed as before.
When truncation removes 3 full lines and does not character-truncate the last visible line, the message reports exactly '3 lines hidden', not '4 lines hidden'.
When truncation removes lines and also character-truncates the final visible line, the hidden line count includes that partially truncated line.
When using '-v' verbosity and the output is near the truncation boundary, the output shown at '-v' is no longer more verbose than what '-vv' would show.
The truncation message correctly uses 'line' (singular) when exactly 1 line is hidden and 'lines' (plural) otherwise.

task_13.title: Fix __tracebackhide__ for chained exceptions
task_13.description: When using __tracebackhide__ in functions that raise chained exceptions (e.g., catching one exception and raising another), the hidden frames were still displayed in the traceback output. The traceback filtering logic did not account for the scenario where all entries in a chained exception's traceback are marked as hidden, causing verbose output instead of the expected clean, user-friendly traceback. This fix ensures that fully-hidden exception chains are properly suppressed from the displayed traceback.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that __tracebackhide__ correctly suppresses traceback frames for chained exceptions (exceptions raised while handling another exception). Previously, when all traceback entries in a chained exception were marked with __tracebackhide__ = True, the frames were still shown in the output, producing verbose tracebacks that defeated the purpose of __tracebackhide__.

expectation.grounded: Traceback.getcrashentry() must return Optional[TracebackEntry], returning None when all traceback entries are hidden rather than falling back to the last entry. ExceptionInfo._getreprcrash() must return Optional[ReprFileLocation], propagating None when no visible crash entry exists. When building the exception representation chain in FormattedExcinfo, if _getreprcrash() returns None (all entries hidden), that segment of the chained exception must be omitted from the representation chain. ReprExceptionInfo.reprcrash must accept Optional[ReprFileLocation] to accommodate fully-hidden tracebacks. For skip exceptions in TestReport, if _getreprcrash() returns None, a ValueError must be raised since skipped tests should always have a visible traceback entry.
expectation.conceptual: When a function sets __tracebackhide__ = True and raises an exception that chains to another exception whose frames are also hidden, the traceback output should be clean and concise — hidden frames must not leak into the displayed traceback. If every frame in a chained exception is hidden, that portion of the chain should be entirely suppressed from the output. The skip-test path should guard against the unexpected case of a fully-hidden skip traceback by raising an error.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not alter traceback display when __tracebackhide__ is not used or when at least one visible entry exists in each part of the chain. The getcrashentry() fallback behavior (previously returning self[-1] when all entries were hidden) must be removed. The skip exception handling in TestReport must explicitly validate that _getreprcrash() returns a non-None value. The ReprExceptionInfo and ReprTraceback data structures should use dataclasses instead of attrs.
constraints.conceptual: Normal traceback rendering for non-hidden frames and unchained exceptions must remain unchanged. The fix must only affect scenarios where all traceback entries in a chained exception segment are marked hidden. Skip-related traceback processing must fail explicitly rather than silently if no crash entry is found.

behavior: Traceback.getcrashentry() returns None instead of the last entry when all traceback entries are hidden via __tracebackhide__
ExceptionInfo._getreprcrash() returns None when getcrashentry() returns None, instead of attempting to access attributes on a non-existent entry
When constructing the exception representation chain, segments where all traceback entries are hidden (reprcrash is None) are omitted from the chain entirely
When style is 'value' and reprcrash exists, the crash location is still suppressed (set to None) in the chain entry, preserving existing 'value' style behavior
ReprExceptionInfo.reprcrash field accepts None to support fully-hidden tracebacks
TestReport raises ValueError when _getreprcrash() returns None during skip exception handling, since skipped tests must always have a visible traceback entry
ReprExceptionInfo and ReprTraceback are converted from attrs classes to dataclasses
acceptance_criteria: Given a function with __tracebackhide__ = True that raises an exception, and a calling function also with __tracebackhide__ = True that catches and re-raises as a different exception type, when a test calls the outer function, then the traceback output should only show the test function's call and the final exception — no hidden frames should appear
Given a simple exception (no chaining) in a function with __tracebackhide__ = True, when a test triggers the exception, then the traceback should be hidden as before (no regression)
Given chained exceptions where some frames are hidden and others are not, when the traceback is rendered, then only the non-hidden frames should appear in the output
Given a chained exception where all traceback entries in one segment are hidden, when the traceback representation chain is built, then that segment should be omitted from the chain
When a skip exception is processed and _getreprcrash() returns None, then a ValueError should be raised indicating that a traceback entry is expected for skip exceptions
When using 'native' traceback style, ReprExceptionInfo should accept a None reprcrash without errors

task_12.title: Fix tmp_path OSError on emscripten platform
task_12.description: The tmp_path fixture unconditionally raised OSError on the emscripten platform because os.getuid() is a stub that always returns 0, causing the temporary directory ownership check to incorrectly fail. The fix introduces a get_user_id() helper that returns None on platforms where getuid() is unreliable (emscripten and win32), allowing the ownership and permission checks to be cleanly skipped on those platforms.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the tmp_path fixture does not raise an OSError on the emscripten platform. Previously, the ownership check for the temporary directory root used os.getuid(), which on emscripten always returns 0 (a stub value), causing the ownership comparison to fail and an OSError to be raised unconditionally. The fixture must correctly handle platforms where os.getuid() is unavailable or unreliable.

expectation.grounded: A get_user_id() utility function must be provided that returns the current user ID as an integer, or None when the platform cannot supply a reliable value. Specifically, it must return None on win32 and emscripten platforms, and also return None if os.getuid() returns -1. When get_user_id() returns None, TempPathFactory must skip the temporary directory ownership check and permission fixup entirely, rather than raising OSError. When get_user_id() returns a valid uid, the existing ownership and permission enforcement must be preserved.
expectation.conceptual: On platforms where the operating system cannot reliably report the current user identity, the temporary path factory must gracefully skip ownership and permission validation instead of raising an error. On platforms that do reliably report user identity, the ownership and permission checks must continue to work as before, raising OSError when the temp directory is not owned by the current user and fixing world-readable permissions.

constraints.grounded: The existing behavior on win32 (skipping ownership checks) must be preserved. The existing behavior on POSIX platforms with a valid getuid() must be preserved: OSError is raised if the temp root directory is not owned by the current user, and world-readable permission bits are stripped. The get_user_id() function must handle the cpython edge case where os.getuid() returns -1 by returning None.
constraints.conceptual: No regression in security posture on platforms that support reliable user identification. The ownership and permission checks must remain active where they were previously enforced. The fix must not introduce new failure modes on any supported platform.

behavior: On emscripten platform, get_user_id() returns None instead of the stub value 0 from os.getuid().
On win32 platform, get_user_id() returns None since os.getuid() is not available.
On standard POSIX platforms, get_user_id() returns the actual user ID from os.getuid().
If os.getuid() returns -1 on any platform, get_user_id() returns None.
When get_user_id() returns None, TempPathFactory skips the ownership check and permission fixup for the temp root directory.
When get_user_id() returns a valid uid, TempPathFactory raises OSError if the temp root directory is owned by a different user.
When get_user_id() returns a valid uid and the temp root has world-readable bits set, those bits are stripped via chmod.
acceptance_criteria: When running on the emscripten platform, requesting the tmp_path fixture should succeed without raising OSError.
When running on win32, the tmp_path fixture should continue to work without performing ownership checks, consistent with prior behavior.
When running on a POSIX platform with a valid user ID, if the temp root directory is owned by a different user, an OSError should be raised indicating the directory is not owned by the current user.
When running on a POSIX platform with a valid user ID, if the temp root directory has world-readable permission bits, those bits should be automatically removed.
When os.getuid() would return -1 (cpython edge case), the tmp_path fixture should succeed without raising OSError.
The get_user_id() function should return an integer on standard POSIX platforms and None on win32 and emscripten.

task_11.title: Fix assertion rewriting for walrus operator expressions
task_11.description: Pytest's assertion rewriting mechanism produced incorrect behavior when assertion expressions contained the walrus operator (:=). Variables reassigned via the walrus operator inside an assert statement would be evaluated incorrectly because the rewriter did not account for in-place variable rebinding during sub-expression evaluation. This caused assertions that passed in plain Python to fail under pytest, or vice versa. The fix ensures that the assertion rewriter correctly tracks variable overwrites caused by named expressions and substitutes temporary variables to preserve the original value for comparison operands.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that assertion expressions containing the walrus operator (:=) behave identically under pytest's assertion rewriting as they do under plain Python execution. Previously, an assert statement such as `assert not np.array_equal(a, a := a.astype(np.uint8))` would pass in normal Python but fail under pytest because the rewriter incorrectly allowed the walrus operator to overwrite the variable before both sides of the comparison were fully evaluated.

expectation.grounded: The AssertionRewriter must implement a visit_NamedExpr visitor that handles ast.NamedExpr nodes (Python 3.8+), producing proper representation of walrus operator targets analogous to visit_Name. A variables_overwrite dictionary must track variables reassigned by walrus operators within an assert. In visit_BoolOp, when a comparison's left operand is a NamedExpr whose target was already referenced in a prior boolean operand, the target must be renamed to a temporary variable. In visit_Compare, the left operand must be substituted with its overwritten temporary name if one exists, and when a NamedExpr on the right side of a comparison would shadow the left operand, the target must be redirected to a fresh temporary variable. The variables_overwrite state must persist across assert statements and not be reset between them.
expectation.conceptual: When a walrus operator reassigns a variable inside an assertion expression, pytest's assertion rewriter must preserve the pre-assignment value for any comparisons or sub-expressions that reference the variable before the assignment point. The rewritten assertion must produce the same truth value and the same intermediate evaluation results as the original assertion would produce under normal Python semantics. Failure messages should correctly display both the original and reassigned values.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not alter assertion rewriting behavior for expressions that do not contain walrus operators. The namedExpr type reference must gracefully degrade on Python versions below 3.8 where ast.NamedExpr does not exist. The variables_overwrite dictionary must not be reset on each new assert statement visit, unlike other per-statement state. Existing visit_Name, visit_Compare, and visit_BoolOp behavior for non-walrus expressions must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Assertions without walrus operators must continue to behave exactly as before. The fix must support all Python versions that pytest targets, gracefully handling the absence of walrus operator syntax on older interpreters. Variable tracking for overwrites must persist correctly across chained or compound assertions.

behavior: When a walrus operator appears as a comparator operand in an assertion (e.g., `assert f(a, a := expr)`), the assertion rewriter now introduces a temporary variable to hold the pre-assignment value so that both sides of the comparison see the correct value.

When a NamedExpr target in a BoolOp has already been referenced by a prior operand, the rewriter renames the target to a temporary variable to prevent the overwrite from corrupting the earlier operand's evaluation.

In visit_Compare, if the left operand's name has been overwritten by a prior walrus assignment tracked in variables_overwrite, the left operand is transparently substituted with the temporary variable name.

The visit_NamedExpr visitor produces repr output for walrus operator targets using the same local-variable and global-name display logic as visit_Name, ensuring assertion failure messages show the walrus-assigned values.
The variables_overwrite state persists across the rewriting of multiple assert statements within the same module, unlike per-statement state which is reset.
acceptance_criteria: When an assertion uses the walrus operator to reassign a variable that is also used as a comparison operand (e.g., `assert not np.array_equal(a, a := a.astype(np.uint8))`), pytest must produce the same pass/fail result as running the same assertion in plain Python.
When a walrus-operator assertion fails, the failure message must correctly display the repr of both the original variable value and the reassigned value.

When a BoolOp assertion contains multiple comparisons where a walrus operator in a later operand reassigns a variable referenced in an earlier operand, each operand must see the correct value of the variable at its evaluation point.
Assertions that do not use the walrus operator must continue to produce identical rewriting behavior and failure output as before the change.
On Python versions below 3.8 (where walrus operator syntax is unavailable), the assertion rewriter must not raise errors or change behavior due to the new NamedExpr handling code.

task_14.title: Fix broken pyproject.toml example in Good Integration Practices documentation
task_14.description: The minimal example pyproject.toml in the 'Good Integration Practices' documentation was missing a required 'version' field under the [project] table. Users following the tutorial and running 'pip install -e .' would encounter a ValueError because modern build backends (e.g., hatchling) require either a static version or an explicit dynamic declaration. The fix adds the missing version entry to the sample pyproject.toml so that the documented workflow succeeds out of the box.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the minimal pyproject.toml example in the 'Good Integration Practices' documentation includes all fields required for a successful editable install. Previously, following the documented steps exactly would cause 'pip install -e .' to fail with a ValueError indicating that 'project.version' could not be resolved.

expectation.grounded: The sample pyproject.toml in the 'Good Integration Practices' guide must include a 'version' key under the [project] table (e.g., version = "0.1.0") alongside the existing 'name' key. With this change, running 'pip install -e .' against a project using the documented example must complete without raising a ValueError related to project.version resolution.
expectation.conceptual: Users who copy the example pyproject.toml from the documentation and run an editable install should succeed without errors. The documentation example must be self-contained and produce a working editable install when followed verbatim.

constraints.grounded: The example must remain minimal — only fields strictly required by the PEP 517/660 build backend (hatchling) should be present. The [build-system] section specifying 'hatchling' as the build-backend and its 'requires' list must be preserved unchanged. No runtime pytest code or configuration is altered.
constraints.conceptual: The documentation fix must not introduce unnecessary complexity into the example. The example should remain the simplest possible valid pyproject.toml that supports editable installs. No runtime behavior of pytest itself is affected by this change.

behavior: The sample pyproject.toml in the Good Integration Practices documentation now contains a static 'version' field under the [project] table.
Running 'pip install -e .' with the corrected example no longer raises a ValueError about project.version resolution.
The documented workflow (create pyproject.toml, run editable install, run pytest) succeeds end-to-end when followed exactly as written.
acceptance_criteria: When a user copies the example pyproject.toml from the Good Integration Practices documentation verbatim, it should contain both 'name' and 'version' fields under [project].
When a user runs 'pip install -e .' in a directory using the documented example pyproject.toml, the editable install should complete successfully without any ValueError.

When following the entire Good Integration Practices tutorial step by step, the user should be able to install the package in editable mode and run pytest against it without encountering build-system errors.
The example pyproject.toml should remain minimal, containing only the [build-system] and [project] sections with the minimum required fields.

task_15.title: Replace attrs dependency with stdlib dataclasses
task_15.description: pytest removed its direct dependency on the third-party attrs package, replacing all internal usage with the Python standard library dataclasses module. This reduces the external dependency footprint for downstream projects. All internal data-holding classes previously decorated with @attr.s are now @dataclasses.dataclass, field definitions use dataclasses.field instead of attr.ib, and serialization helpers use dataclasses.asdict instead of attr.asdict. Converter logic previously handled by attrs is now performed explicitly at construction sites or in __post_init__ methods. Slots previously declared via attrs are now explicit __slots__ declarations. Nice diffs for user-defined attrs classes remain supported.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest no longer requires the attrs package as a direct dependency. All internal classes that previously used attrs decorators and utilities must be migrated to use the standard library dataclasses module. The migration must preserve the existing public API contracts, including class construction signatures, field defaults, frozen/immutable semantics, equality behavior, serialization via asdict, and repr output. Converter logic previously handled implicitly by attrs field converters must continue to normalize inputs (e.g., converting iterables to tuples, coercing path arguments to strings). Downstream plugins and test suites must not experience regressions in exception reporting, mark handling, fixture definitions, parametrization, caching, temporary directory management, or test result serialization/deserialization.

expectation.grounded: All internal classes (ExceptionInfo, FormattedExcinfo, TerminalRepr, ExceptionRepr, ExceptionChainRepr, ReprExceptionInfo, ReprTraceback, ReprEntryNative, ReprEntry, ReprFileLocation, ReprLocals, ReprFuncArgs, TempPathFactory, TempdirFactory, _PytestWrapper, Config.InvocationParams, WarningReport, PseudoFixtureDef, FuncFixtureInfo, FixtureFunctionMarker, CallInfo, KeywordMatcher, MarkMatcher, Mark, MarkDecorator, Token, IdMaker, CallSpec2, Skip, Xfail, Cache, _bestrelpath_cache, UnformattedWarning) must use @dataclasses.dataclass instead of @attr.s. Field definitions must use dataclasses.field() instead of attr.ib()/attr.Factory(). Serialization in _report_to_json and _report_kwargs_from_json must use dataclasses.asdict() instead of attr.asdict(). Frozen dataclasses (Mark, Config.InvocationParams, CallSpec2, IdMaker, PseudoFixtureDef, FixtureFunctionMarker, Skip, Xfail, Token) must remain immutable. Classes that previously used attrs slots=True (KeywordMatcher, MarkMatcher, FuncFixtureInfo, _bestrelpath_cache, Token, Xfail, CallSpec2, IdMaker) must declare explicit __slots__. ExceptionRepr field order must place reprtraceback before reprcrash. ReprExceptionInfo.reprcrash must accept Optional[ReprFileLocation]. ReprFileLocation must coerce its path argument to str via __post_init__. Config.InvocationParams must convert args from Iterable[str] to Tuple[str, ...] in its __init__. FixtureFunctionMarker must accept a _ispytest init-only variable and validate it via check_ispytest in __post_init__, with tuple conversion of params and ids done at the fixture() call site. ExceptionChainRepr must extract reprtraceback and reprcrash from the last chain element during __init__ and pass them to the parent ExceptionRepr constructor.
expectation.conceptual: pytest must function identically after replacing its internal attrs usage with dataclasses. All data-holding classes must preserve their construction interfaces, immutability guarantees, equality semantics, and serialization behavior. Input normalization (type coercion, tuple conversion) that was previously implicit via attrs converters must still occur. Exception representation, test reporting, mark/fixture handling, parametrization, caching, skip/xfail evaluation, and temporary directory management must all behave the same as before the migration. The attrs package must no longer appear in pytest's direct dependency list.

constraints.grounded: The attrs package must not be imported by any pytest internal module. Classes with eq=False in their attrs decorator must use dataclass(eq=False) to preserve identity-based equality. Classes that were frozen must remain frozen via dataclass(frozen=True). The _args_converter helper function is removed; its tuple-conversion logic must be preserved in Config.InvocationParams.__init__ using object.__setattr__ for frozen assignment. The _params_converter and _ensure_immutable_ids converters are removed; their normalization must be preserved at the fixture() function call site. attr.asdict must not be called anywhere; dataclasses.asdict must be used for report serialization. Keyword arguments must be used when constructing ReprExceptionInfo to match the new dataclass field ordering. Nice diffs for user-defined attrs classes in test output must continue to be supported.
constraints.conceptual: The migration must not change any user-facing behavior or public API. Internal class instantiation order and field semantics must be preserved. No new external dependencies may be introduced. Input validation and type coercion previously handled by attrs must still be enforced. Serialization and deserialization of test reports must remain backward-compatible. Immutability and equality contracts on all affected classes must be maintained.

behavior: All internal data classes use @dataclasses.dataclass instead of @attr.s, with matching frozen, eq, and repr settings
Field defaults and factories use dataclasses.field(default_factory=...) instead of attr.Factory(...)
Classes that had attrs slots=True now declare explicit __slots__ tuples
attr.asdict() calls in report serialization are replaced with dataclasses.asdict()
ExceptionRepr field order changed: reprtraceback is now declared before reprcrash
ReprExceptionInfo.reprcrash type broadened from ReprFileLocation to Optional[ReprFileLocation]
ExceptionChainRepr uses an explicit __init__ that extracts reprtraceback and reprcrash from the last chain element and passes them to the parent constructor via super().__init__()
ReprFileLocation coerces its path argument to str in __post_init__ instead of using an attrs converter
Config.InvocationParams converts args from Iterable[str] to Tuple[str, ...] in a custom __init__ using object.__setattr__ on the frozen instance
FixtureFunctionMarker gains a _ispytest init-only field validated in __post_init__; params and ids tuple conversion moved to the fixture() call site
The _args_converter standalone function is removed from the config module
The attrs package import is removed from all pytest internal modules
ReprExceptionInfo and other classes now require keyword arguments at certain construction sites due to dataclass field reordering
acceptance_criteria: When installing pytest 7.3.0, the attrs package must not be listed as a direct dependency
When a test fails with an exception chain, ExceptionChainRepr must correctly extract reprtraceback and reprcrash from the last element in the chain and display the full chain
When serializing test reports via _report_to_json, dataclasses.asdict must be used and the output format must be identical to the previous attrs-based serialization
When deserializing test reports via _report_kwargs_from_json, ReprExceptionInfo must be constructable with keyword arguments reprtraceback and reprcrash
When creating a frozen dataclass instance such as Mark, Config.InvocationParams, or CallSpec2, attempting to modify attributes after construction must raise FrozenInstanceError
When constructing Config.InvocationParams with args as a list, the args attribute must be stored as a tuple
When constructing ReprFileLocation with a Path object as the path argument, the path attribute must be coerced to a string
When defining a fixture via @pytest.fixture, the FixtureFunctionMarker must validate _ispytest and correctly convert params and ids to tuples
When using dataclass classes that previously had slots=True (e.g., KeywordMatcher, MarkMatcher, Token, Xfail), the __slots__ declaration must prevent dynamic attribute assignment
When pytest formats exception output for classes with eq=False (TerminalRepr and its subclasses), equality comparison must remain identity-based rather than value-based
When users define their own test classes using attrs, pytest must still produce nice diffs in assertion output
